job.title: Part-Time / On-Call Registered Social Worker
job.description:
The New Normal Charity Hong Kong is a registered Section 88 charity dedicated to supporting adults through life's most difficult moments. The organization focuses on making mental health and community resources accessible to individuals who may be facing financial hardship and emotional distress, in a city where many live in poverty and lack adequate support. It offers free peer-to-peer support groups, holistic well-being programs, and mental health-related training to ensure people receive timely and appropriate help. Guided by the belief that no one should face challenges alone, The New Normal Charity builds inclusive, compassionate support networks across Hong Kong.

Interested individuals and partners can connect with the organisation via hello@thenewnormalcharityhk.org.

The New Normal Charity Hong Kong is seeking a Part-Time / On-Call Registered Social Worker at the ASWO level to provide professional clinical backing for our peer support community.
 
We require a qualified professional to deliver expert safeguarding, triage and referral, and immediate crisis intervention when rare high-risk situations arise. This role ensures that while peer facilitators host our support groups, they have direct access to professional guidance to keep participants protected and appropriately cared for.
 
In this role, you will be on standby during nine evening peer support groups per month to provide remote intervention and guide facilitators. Beyond active group hours, you will conduct up to nine hours of post-group follow-up per month, completing intake assessments and connecting service users to other appropriate supports. You will also debrief facilitators following safeguarding incidents, maintain documentation, and collaborate with our Designated Safeguarding Lead to refine institutional policies and reporting.
 
Your Duties
On-Call Group Standby
Be on standby/on-call during our scheduled peer support groups (9 groups per month, 2.5 hours per group, total of 22.5 hours) to assist peer facilitators in handling safeguarding concerns, immediate crisis escalation or high-risk situations.
Our groups are scheduled on weekdays 7.30pm to 9.00pm. You would commence on call 30 minutes before doors open and remain available for 30 minutes after. Outside the standby window, volunteers follow TN's standing escalation protocol and there is no expectation that you will be contactable.

Risk Assessments and Crisis Intervention
Conduct immediate, professional risk assessments and crisis intervention remotely for service users who are identified as high risk during groups. Provide instructions to peer facilitators on group containment and emergency response.

Ad-Hoc Follow-up and Referrals: Provide time-limited follow-up to service users post-group. Maintain a referral network, conduct intakes and referrals to other services such as clinical psychologists, psychiatrists, or community mental health services (ordinarily up to 9 hours per month).

Facilitator Support and Documentation: Debrief with peer facilitators post-session when safeguarding concerns occur to ensure their well-being and safety. Maintain and update incident documentation on TN's systems and templates.
Incident Review, Audit and Enhancement: Support the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) and Head of Programmes to complete review and report of incidents to the Board, and enhance policy and service delivery. Perform other duties reasonably ancillary to the safeguarding function, such as training, protocol review and administration, as agreed with the Head of Programmes.
 
What we are looking for
  • Professional Credentials: Must be a Registered Social Worker (RSW) in Hong Kong with a Bachelor's Degree in Social Work or above (ASWO equivalent qualification). Completed training in safeguarding, crisis intervention or suicide prevention.Willing and able to produce necessary certification/ documentation of qualification. Current registration is a continuing condition of engagement: you must maintain registration throughout, permit annual verification against the Social Workers Registration Board register, and notify TNN immediately if your registration lapses or becomes subject to conditions or disciplinary proceedings.
  • Experience: At least 2 years of post-qualification social work experience, preferably in mental health. Experience managing in-person or remote on-call support during high-risk situations, including those at risk of suicide or in acute crisis.
  • Skills: Strong skills in rapid triage, risk assessments, support, and navigating Hong Kong's emergency services and public/ private referral networks. Ability to support peer facilitators in challenging interactions.
  • Communication: Fluent in written and spoken Cantonese and English.
  • Attributes: Resilient and emotionally composed under pressure, empathetic and highly adaptive, and comfortable working in a small charity environment.
  • Pre-engagement Checks: Any offer is conditional on satisfactory verification of RSW registration, two professional references, and a self-declaration of criminal convictions and professional disciplinary history.
 
Your Impact
 
Many people in Hong Kong struggle with life's challenges, often feeling isolated and uncertain about where to turn for help. By stepping into this role, you directly ensure that peer support remains a safe, sustainable space for over 1,000 people navigating life's most difficult moments in Hong Kong.

Your professional expertise bridges the gap between community support and formal mental healthcare for over 1,000 people across Hong Kong. By providing immediate clinical guidance during crises and clear referral pathways, you empower volunteer facilitators to lead with confidence, ensure vulnerable individuals get the care they need, and keep peer support safe and sustainable.
 
What we offer
 The pay for this role is benchmarked against the Hong Kong Government Master Pay Scale (MPS) Point 16 (ASWO starting point):
* Fixed monthly salary: HK$4,995 / month
* This base amount is guaranteed each month simply for being on call and available during our core group hours, regardless of whether a crisis occurs.
* Ad-hoc overtime: HK$222 / hour for any active follow-up, risk assessments, or referral paperwork triggered by a group incident (capped at 9 hours / HK$1,998 per month).
* Total Monthly Earning Potential: Up to HK$6,993 / month.
* Initial contract duration is one year, reviewable.
* Employees' Compensation Insurance (ECI): In compliance with Hong Kong law, the successful candidate will be fully covered under TN's Employees' Compensation Insurance for all working and standby hours.
* Public Liability Insurance (PLI): TNN provides comprehensive Public Liability Insurance covering all employees, volunteers, and peer support group participants across our venues.
* Professional Indemnity Insurance (PII): As this role involves providing professional risk assessments and clinical referral pathways, the candidate is required to maintain their own active Professional Indemnity Insurance (PI) and provide a copy of the policy certificate upon contract signing. (Note: TNN is happy to discuss a reasonable annual subsidy/reimbursement toward the cost of your personal Pll policy).
* Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF): Standard MPF contributions are provided

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
Shakespeare4All Company Limited (S4A) was founded in 2003 and is a charity registered under S88. It is recognised throughout Hong Kong for its spectacular annual Shakespeare Gala production, supported by founding sponsor SWIRE Properties and has provided drama experiences to thousands of students from aided, direct subsidy, government and private schools in the region. At its inception, S4A pursued a very specific manifesto of using Shakespearean text to support confidence in English. However, in recent years the organisation has evolved to work on a larger platform, providing diverse performance and learning opportunities to children and youth along with professional support. We are also true to the ‘4All’ part of our moniker by reaching out into communities to work with students and students with different abilities from all over Hong Kong.

It is our mission to inspire young people to aspire to excellence:
INSPIRE: Offering a learning environment that is creative, original and structured
ASPIRE: A demanding but imaginative framework that involves new thinking and disciplines
EXCELLENCE: Drawing out the potential in students to be the best they can be

Project Manager
(Initial six-month term, with potential extension on an annual basis for three years.)

We are now looking for candidates with the following skills and attributes:
● Hong Kong Permanent Resident or with a valid working visa
● Degree holders majoring in arts management, arts and humanities or equivalent qualifications/experience
● Bilingual speaker with ability to write in Chinese
● Minimum 3 years of experience in arts administration
● Passionate about theatre, arts education and youth development
● Able to multi-tasks, work under pressure and willing to take up challenges
● Responsible, attention to detail and organised
● Experience in professional theatre production/school touring shows is an advantage
● Excellent leadership and communication skills
● Prepared to travel around Hong Kong to participating schools of the programme
● Prepared to work weekends, nighttime occasionally to accommodate production schedules
● Proficiency in computer applications (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
● Other computer skills are an advantage

Responsibilities:
● Manage, oversee, and monitor the general procurement function and activities to ensure that the projects and procedures are implemented and adhered to
● Initiate, communicate and work smoothly with members at all levels in the project team, contractors and other stakeholders
● Interact and liaise with sponsor(s) or other organisations in relation to claims management on the project
● Review plans and submissions for all projects as well as the implementation of such plans and submissions
● Work alongside with the Head Tutor to manage in-school programmes
● Report to the Artistic Director, General Manager and Deputy General Manager on operations

Please send your CV in confidence, all information will be treated with the strictest confidence.

job.title: Chair, Board of Directors
job.description:
ROLE PURPOSE – CHAIR, BOARD OF DIRECTORS, THE FRED HOLLOWS FOUNDATION (HONG KONG)


OUR VISION
A world in which no person is needlessly blind or vision impaired.

OUR PURPOSE
We are determined to deliver Fred Hollows’ vision of preventing blindness and restoring sight.

Our priority is to work with communities to improve their own eye health. We do this through life-changing surgeries and treatments, training doctors and health workers, generating new ideas, and pushing for change at all levels – from local to global. The Foundation works in more than 25 developing in East Asia, South Asia and the Middle East, Africa and Australasia.

The Fred Hollows Foundation (“The Foundation”) established the Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) over a decade ago, and together with other international organisations in the United Kingdom, Kenya and the United States of America, the international organisations form a global network to support the work of The Foundation. The Foundation’s latest Annual Report is available here and the Global Strategy 2024-2028 is available here.

ROLE PURPOSE
The Chair leads The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) (FHF (HK)) Board of Directors to achieve its aim: ending avoidable blindness and restoring sight to those in need.

Within the global Fred Hollows Foundation network, FHF HK plays a primary role in mobilising resources (as a ‘market entity’) to support sight-restoring work in low- and middle-income countries.

By 2030, FHF HK aspires to be The Foundation’s trusted catalyst of resourcing for the Greater China Region, unlocking resources, partnerships and influence to scale eye health equity across Asia. FHF HK will do this by serving as The Foundation’s regional philanthropy hub in Greater China, mobilising capital (donations, institutional philanthropy and investment), partnerships and influence across Hong Kong and Macau to scale eye health impact.

The Chair plays a critical role in ensuring effective governance leadership, strong strategic oversight, and alignment with The Foundation’s vision of a world in which no one is needlessly blind. The Chair also leverages their networks to unlock access to prospective significant supporters and facilitates engagement with priority stakeholders and events that would not otherwise be accessible to FHF HK.

With the term of the current Chair concluding at the end of November 2026, it is suggested that a new Chair be appointed in the lead up to the expiry of the current Chair’s term.

Role of The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) Chair
The Chair of the Board of The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) is appointed by the Board of Directors, with Directors approved by the Global Board of the sole member (The Foundation).

The Chair serves for two three-year terms. Directors may serve a maximum of nine consecutive years. The powers of Directors, the Board and its Chair are set out in the Articles of Association and the Corporate Governance Charter.

The Chair is expected to:
1. Ensure, in partnership with the Board, that FHF HK’s strategy is aligned with The Foundation’s Vision and Strategy, and that goals are achieved with integrity.
2. Promote the values and goals of The Foundation in all aspects of governance and engagement with members, employees, partners, governments and communities.
3. Perform duties in alignment with The Foundation’s Charter, the Articles of Association and relevant law, ensuring FHF HK operates in an ethically, environmentally and socially responsible manner.
4. Lead the Board with tact and diplomacy, promoting a culture of integrity, respect, transparency, collaboration, resourcefulness and compliance.
5. Chair Board meetings to ensure they are effective, efficient, and support high-quality, ethical decision-making.
6. Commit sufficient time to the role, including representing FHF HK at donor, corporate, government and community engagements, and providing access to professional and philanthropic networks.
7. Build a productive working relationship with management, including the Head of Market Hong Kong and Macau and relevant Global teams, including setting Board agendas.
8. Engage with The Foundation’s initiatives to evolve global governance frameworks.

Essential Experience
1. Demonstrated experience to Chair the Board.
2. Demonstrated ability to implement and oversee governance, integrity and compliance processes at a board level.
3. Demonstrated ability to lead and implement change.
4. Demonstrated ability to develop substantial philanthropic, business or corporate fundraising networks and relationships on behalf of The Foundation and take part in high level meetings.

Desirable Experience
1. Demonstrated experience negotiating and partnering with not-for-profits, corporations, governments, multi-lateral and other non-government agencies in pursuit of The Foundation’s goals and interests.
2. Understanding of how a brand is perceived in the market and execution of brand management
3. Experience working with an international health and development organisation.
4. Demonstrated understanding of working with developing countries and human rights.
5. An established public profile known for credible authentic leadership with access to high level decision makers in government and industry

Skills
1. Strategic leadership and organisational stewardship.
2. Governance, financial and risk oversight expertise.
3. Effective board leadership and facilitation.
4. Political acumen, influence and relational leadership.
5. Sharp analysis and sound judgment in complex and ambiguous environments.
6. Diplomacy, negotiation and partnership capability.
7. Ability to operate across diverse cultures and contexts.

Qualifications
Relevant qualifications in leadership and Company Directors Course and MBA or Bachelor of Commerce/Economics/Business Management/Political Science/Law degree or equivalent.

Attributes
1. Strong commitment to The Fred Hollows Foundation’s vision and values.
2. Hong Kong residency preferred; experience in international or cross-cultural organisations desirable.
3. Mandarin language proficiency preferred but not essential.

Safeguarding
The Chair will be required to undertake training and sign up to the standards set for conduct by The Foundation, the Australian Government’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian NGO Co-operation Program and the Australian Council for International Development. This includes child protection and prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

Travel
Domestic and International travel may be required as part of this role.

TIME COMMITMENT
· Up to four Board meetings per year (two hours).
· Up to one budget briefing per year (1-2 hours).
· Up to two International Organisation meetings per year (1-2 hours).
· Ongoing agenda setting and governance preparation.
· Regular stakeholder engagement, including donor, partner and advocacy events.

TERM OF APPOINTMENT
Appointed for an initial term of three years, renewable once by mutual agreement between FHF HK and The Foundation for a maximum term of 6 years.

APPOINTMENT STRUCTURE
Board Director roles for The Foundation are voluntary (unpaid). The role offers the opportunity to contribute at a strategic level to a globally recognised organisation, shaping the growth of the Hong Kong market and enabling eye health programs that restore sight and transform lives and communities globally.

job.title: Programme Manager
job.description:
Environmental non-profit Redress is looking for a Programme Manager to deliver a 1-year project from September 2026 to August 2027. The ‘Value Wardrobe’ project aims to empower senior secondary students from low-income families to become informed, financially capable, and responsible fashion consumers through education and experiential learning. The project addresses fast fashion overconsumption by strengthening financial literacy, sustainable decision-making, and future-ready skills. The project includes 3 key elements: school talks, skills development workshops and the organisation of a student-led secondhand festival in Sham Shui Po. The project will be mainly delivered in Cantonese. 

This role will suit an energetic person with excellent people and communication skills, strong teaching skills and a passion for youth education and sustainability. 

PRINCIPLE RESPONSIBILITIES 

  • Manage the project timeline and delivery of the planned activities to ensure achievement of the set KPIs and budget 

  • Handle the outreach and communication with partners, including guest speakers, school principals, teachers, students, and various vendors for the Festival 

  • Lead on the educational direction of the project, including developing the content for workshops and monitoring the content to be delivered by external speakers

  • Deliver the workshops, activities and the Festival 
 
  • Establish data tracking mechanisms to record impact data as well as spendings, and ensure on-time reporting to the funder 

  • In close collaboration with the Communications team, devise a communication plan and propose content for promotion of the project (social media, website, etc) and especially that of the Festival 

  • As part of the Redress team, supports the wider activities, e.g. the bi-annual pop-up shops 


Main reporting line: Circular Fashion Programme Director

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS,  & EXPERIENCE:
 
  • Undergraduate university degree
  • Minimum 3 years relevant working experience 
  • Experience working with schools, students, teachers, educators or curriculum development is a must
  • Existing connections within the local school network in Hong Kong will be a plus
  • Strong project management skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in both Cantonese and English
  • Passion for sustainability and education 
  • Eligible to live and work in Hong Kong 
Benefits: 
  • 2-day work from home arrangement
  • 20 days annual leave 
  • 25% off in our secondhand shop 
  • Salary and MPF are fixed according to the grant 


To apply, please send the following to aurianne@redress.com.hk : 

  • Your CV
  • Your expected salary 
  • Your earliest available start date 

Please kindly note that applications through Linkedin won’t be taken into consideration

ABOUT REDRESS

Redress is a Hong Kong-based environmental NGO on a mission to accelerate the transition to a circular fashion industry by educating and empowering designers and consumers, in order to reduce clothing’s negative environmental impacts. Although our work has global reach, we are proudly Asia focused. 
 
Our programmes primarily target fashion designers and consumers. We also work with brands, manufacturers, research institutions, schools, nonprofits, and corporations. We work to create better ways to design, produce, purchase, reuse, and recycle clothing.
 
https://redress.com.hk/

job.title: Program Manager
job.description:
Summerbridge Hong Kong, established in 1992, is a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the educational trajectories of underprivileged students through tuition-free, high-quality English language education and life skills development. The organization provides a supportive learning environment that helps students build confidence, communication skills, and broader opportunities for their future. Summerbridge Hong Kong also engages student teachers, offering them meaningful teaching experience that promotes cross-cultural exchange and community engagement. By combining student learning with educator development, the organization advances both educational equity and civic responsibility in Hong Kong SAR.
Summerbridge Hong Kong Program Manager

Program Managers share full operational and administrative responsibility for the organization’s programs. Their responsibilities include supervising students and staff as well as maintaining contact with and supporting the organization’s growing alumni body. Program Managers are also active in student and staff recruitment, staff training, fiscal management, fund raising and curriculum development. During the summer, each Program Manager is directly responsible for running one of the organization’s Summer Programs.

Priority Mission:
1. Design, Implement and Promote an exceptional, high quality Summerbridge Program with idealistic vision, high spirit, and cohesive team environment.
2. Define, question, redefine and enhance what it means to be “Exceptional.”

Responsibilities of the Program Managers include but are not limited to:

(**Priority Responsibilities )

School Year Programs & School Year Responsibilities
**Study, research and analyze fundamental issues facing Summerbridge and construct an idealistic and visionary plan for the summer program.
**Assist in Fund Raising Process
Attend prospect meetings set up by Board members. Explain and promote the Summerbridge Program to them
Follow up with any information the prospects may need
**Be responsible for all preparation work leading up to the Summer Program including staff recruitment and student recruitment
**Conduct presentations at schools to recruit staff and students.
**Recruit leadership team and ensure they embody the spirit and leadership skills required to carry out vision for summer program.
**Recruit new and returning staff and ensure they embody the spirit and values of Summerbridge or have high potential to comprehend and execute it. Look for staff that are mature and will be supportive of each other. Look for staff that are sincerely interested in helping students and advancing the Summerbridge mission. Form a view on what other important criteria and characteristics are required for assembling the highest quality team.
**Co-coordinate school year programs: Summerbridge-After-School, and Sponsor Field
Trips
**Promote positive and enjoyable working culture in the Summerbridge office
**Promote active communication. Promote culture of attacking problems early and solving them.
Evaluate all aspects of the School Year Programs for effectiveness, and implement improvements where needed
Co-organize training sessions for the school year program staff
Co-organize classroom observation, evaluation, and feedback sessions for all programs
**Manage the programs’ finances to ensure all expenditures are in line with the budget

Summer Program
Refer to ‘Priority Mission’
Effectively utilize all resources including Summerbridge Board, , FTs, Staff, etc. to achieve mission.
**Research and determine essential elements and curriculum for Staff orientation.
**Design program to teach students “Essential Skills” for success including but not limited to: Critical Thinking skills, Study skills, English Language Development, Values/Ethics, Goal setting, Social Skills, Confidence. Further evaluate and determine what “Essential” skills should include.
**Inspire and lead staff to reach full potential. Encourage teamwork. Inspire staff to focus on ‘bigger picture.’ Instill confidence as well as sense of purpose and passion in staff.
**Have Fun and make sure the program is Fun.
**Delegate responsibilities effectively. Try to deliver delegations in the context of personal growth and leadership opportunities
**Promote active communication. Promote culture of attacking problems early and solving them.
**Promote cultural sensitivity. Promote safe environment where students and staff can take risks and grow personally
Integrate auxiliary programs into the Summer Program including the Future Teacher Program and the Returning Student Program
Evaluate programs’ effectiveness and consistently implement improvements
**Manage Any Student Issues that may arise

Summerbridge Website
Initiate the Improvement and Development of the Summerbridge website.

Curriculum Development
**Evaluate the definition of and effectiveness of the organization’s “Essential Skills” curriculum and make improvements
Evaluate the essential elements of a successfully taught class. Set goals, and help teachers procure resources to achieve them

Staff Recruitment, Support & Training
**Co-coordinate the local and overseas staff recruitment process.
Coordinate with Breakthrough Collaborative/Summerbridge National in the recruiting process
Evaluate and improve the Staff Handbook and other training material sent to staff before the summer and school year programs
Design and implement staff workshops, both academic and non-academic, that are to be run by sites and programs
Recruit Deans of Faculty and Mentor Teachers for Summer Program
Plan and implement Dean of Faculty and Mentor Teacher Orientation and training
Coordinate with other organizations to provide staff with professional expertise in the areas inadequately covered by program staff and administrators
**Design teacher training workshops covering program-related issues (e.g., student and staff diversity, cultural sensitivity, issues facing local students, etc.)

Student Recruitment
Co-manage student recruitment process including application design, distribution, review, and follow-up
Research and make recommendation on the optimal student body. (I.e. What mix of students body, demographically and socio-economically, enable Summerbridge to have the highest impact in terms of the following: Helping the community, targeting underprivileged students, creating diverse student body, spotting and cultivating future leaders of Summerbridge.) Suggest on any other goals.
Design and organize recruitment presentations at local schools
Work closely with school contacts and social workers to identify students appropriate for the program

Student Support
**Serve as, and encourage other staff to serve as, an educational and personal resource to students and families
Develop and maintain a system of documenting students’ progress
Coordinate meetings with professional social workers where necessary
Establish and maintain contact with relevant community organizations to develop social, emotional, and academic support and resources outside of Summerbridge
Communicate regularly with Contact Schools to follow-up with school year issues
Prepare recommendations for students and staff applying for other educational or vocational opportunities
Arrange parent conferences where necessary

Alumni Services
Establish and maintain lines of communication with alumni (e.g., alumni database)
Initiate and help coordinate alumni events
Research and compile information on opportunities, organizations and services that may be of interest to alumni (e.g., scholarships, alternatives to Forms 6-7, overseas universities, community service and youth leadership opportunities, etc.)

Contact School Relations
Organize annual visits to Contact Schools to meet with school principals, teachers, and social workers
Coordinate all communication with school contacts regarding Summerbridge programs and activities
Identify and recruit potential new contact schools for student recruitment purposes

Parent Relations
Promote communication between Summerbridge and parents through newsletters, phone calls, parent conferences, etc.
Organize opportunities for parents to become involved in the summer and school year programs

Host School Development Relations
Coordinate with Board to identify and solicit potential host schools for both the summer and school year programs
Coordinate communication to and from potential and existing host schools leading up to the summer and school year programs
Communicate regularly with the host schools’ administrative and maintenance staff to coordinate the use of facilities and develop a positive working relationship
Communicate and enforce the expectations laid out in the Summerbridge Host School Contract

Evaluation: Assessment
Design and implement assessment procedures to track students’ progress

**Note: It is not expected for the PM to handle all these responsibilities alone. In good Summerbridge spirit, a number of these responsibilities should be tackled as a team. It is incumbent upon the PM to cultivate a strong and effective team environment during the school year and during the summer.

Also, the PM should maintain an open dialogue with the Executive Director to discuss and question Mission and Responsibilities. The Team welcomes and encourages suggestions of improvements regarding priorities, definitions and implementation methodologies. All responsibilities should be implemented with the core Mission in mind.

This post is on a 1-year contract basis
